title: Release manifest: release identity and service-manager termination grace
description: Reviewed record naming the chain and block the cutover happens at, and binding the external service-manager termination grace to the client's compiled protocol bounds. Schema validation alone is never sufficient: the document must also pass `keep-client release-manifest validate`, which re-derives every number from the compiled bounds of the exact release binary and holds the recorded chain id and cutover block against what that binary compiles in. A release-acceptance decision additionally requires `validate --release-ready`, which refuses a manifest whose cutover block is still the zero placeholder. What the release was built into — the commit and the image digests — is deliberately not here: those are outputs of a build over this document's own bytes, so recording them would require this tree to contain a hash of itself. They live in the detached release provenance (release-provenance.schema.json), generated after the build and checked against this document by `release-manifest verify-provenance`.

release_identity.description: What chain and block the reviewed cutover is for. Both are checked against the client's compiled constants by every validate run. Build outputs are not recorded here; see the detached release provenance.

chain_id.description: Chain id the compiled mainnet cutover block is for. Validation re-derives it from the same network definition the client verifies the remote endpoint against at connect time.

cutover_block.description: Mainnet cutover block C. Must equal participation.MainnetCutoverBlock as compiled into the release binary, so the reviewed document can never publish a height no node observes. Zero is the compiled placeholder and is refused by `--release-ready`.

tbtc_completion_blocks.description: tbtc.MaximumLegacyCompletionBlocks(): the longest already-started tBTC work may legitimately run, in blocks.

beacon_completion_blocks.description: beacon.MaximumLegacyCompletionBlocks(config): the longest already-started beacon work may legitimately run, in blocks.

beacon_inputs.description: The beacon chain configuration the beacon bound was derived from, for reviewer retracing.

maximum_legacy_completion_blocks.description: max(tbtc, beacon) completion bound: the starting input of both the in-process backstop and the external grace.

reviewed_margin_blocks.description: Reviewed block margin absorbing chain-clock jitter around the completion bound (quiesceReviewedMarginBlocks).

upper_block_interval_seconds.description: Conservative upper bound on the Ethereum block interval used for the block-to-wall-clock conversion (quiesceUpperBlockIntervalSeconds).

rpc_processing_allowance_seconds.description: RPC and processing skew allowance inside the in-process backstop (quiesceBackstopMargin).

in_process_backstop_seconds.description: (maximum_legacy_completion_blocks + reviewed_margin_blocks) * upper_block_interval_seconds + rpc_processing_allowance_seconds — the deadline quiesceBackstopDeadline() arms in the client.

forced_cancellation_allowance_seconds.description: Compiled allowance (compiledForcedCancellationAllowanceSeconds) the runtime's forced-cancellation cleanup wait consumes, covering the audited path between the backstop firing and SIGKILL. Compiled-bound validation rejects any recorded value other than that constant — a manifest can never grant a cleanup window the running process does not observe. Must be positive: the external grace must end strictly after the in-process backstop.

process_exit_headroom_seconds.description: Compiled reviewed headroom (processExitHeadroomSeconds) for the shutdown work outside both in-process timers: controller scheduling and the quiesce call before the backstop arms, the gate close between the timers, and the logging, teardown, and process exit after them. Must be positive: the service manager counts the grace from signal delivery, so a grace equal to the two timed waits alone leaves that work unbudgeted.

termination_grace_period_seconds.description: in_process_backstop_seconds + forced_cancellation_allowance_seconds + process_exit_headroom_seconds — the exact value deployment scaffolds must configure (Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds, systemd TimeoutStopSec).
